title: Ephemeral bootstrap roles and TF state locking to prevent parallel-tenant provisioning races
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds ephemeral bootstrap roles for tenant provisioning, central TF state locking options, helm hook updates to ensure idempotent tenant CRD creation, and a post-provision reconciler that removes temporary privileges. No user-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: In large on-prem/private installs we saw race conditions during parallel tenant provisioning. Multiple bootstrap workers could attempt to create identical tenant-scoped IAM roles and run overlapping terraform apply operations against the same remote state, causing apply conflicts and intermittent install failures. This PR introduces a safer, idempotent bootstrap flow: 1) the installer requests a short-lived (24h by default) bootstrap role per-tenant which is created with a unique suffix; 2) terraform modules are updated to use a central locking backend (S3+Dynamo/Consul/Postgres supported) and expose a lock namespace per-tenant; 3) helm charts add pre-install hooks that gate CRD/namespace creation and requeue if lock unavailable; 4) a reconciler process runs after successful provision to revoke/delete ephemeral roles and emit a permanent tenant role binding (if configured). The change set covers terraform modules, helm hooks, policy bundle generation templates, and the installer orchestration with a migration path. What changed: - Terraform: new module tenant-bootstrap now accepts bootstrap_role_name, lock_backend, lock_namespace and can run in a dry-run idempotent mode. Added state locking examples and a small migration script to move state with minimal downtime. - Helm: charts/private/templates/hooks.yaml adds a pre-install hook that obtains a lock before applying tenant-scoped resources and retries transient lock failures. Added values for lock config. - Policy bundle generator: emit per-tenant temporary role templates and include ttl metadata so the reconciler can identify and rotate them. - Installer: bootstrap coordinator creates ephemeral roles using the policy generator, records bootstrap metadata to installer-state, calls terraform with lock namespace, waits for success then triggers post-provision reconciler to convert ephemeral role to long-lived bindings where required and revoke leftover permissions. - Scripts: tools/migrate-bootstrap-roles.sh to migrate existing installs that used the old global bootstrap role into the new per-tenant ephemeral model. - Docs: docs/upgrade-rollback.md updated with explicit rollback steps in case terraform apply cannot acquire a lock. Checklist: - [x] Design reviewed (ENG-1024) - [x] Terraform module unit tests - [x] Helm lint + integration k8s smoke tests - [x] Policy bundle template unit tests - [x] Migration script tested on internal staging cluster - [x] Rollback playbook documented Rollout plan: staged rollout. 1) Merge to main and tag canary release. 2) Enable new flow behind feature flag in private-installer. 3) Run migration script for customers that opted in. 4) Monitor metrics/alerts for provisioning failures and excessive role creation. 5) Flip feature flag once stable. Backwards compatibility: existing installs that don't opt into the new flow keep using the global bootstrap role. The migration script automates switching an install to the new model. Security considerations: ephemeral roles have a limited TTL and minimal scope; reconciler ensures revoke on success/failure; audit events are emitted to installer audit log. Performance: small additional latency while acquiring locks under high contention; perf mitigation includes exponential backoff and configurable lock timeouts. Testing: unit tests for terraform templates, CI e2e canary against staging, and manual smoke on a 50-tenant parallel create scenario where we validated no conflicts in 50 concurrent runs. Known limitations: If the lock backend is misconfigured, installs may block rather than fail; docs call out supported backends and troubleshooting steps. Merge notes: squash and merge, bumped module versions and added migration script to tools/.
